name: RVRL Thursday Night Rage (8 June 2006)

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline: Little Rock Civic Center, 8 June 2006.

appearances.source: Named as RVRL's presiding president in the broadcast's own staff introduction.
Hosted and called the entire broadcast.
Accompanied Aries Priest to the ring and interfered in his matches.
Ran in from the crowd to aid Colt Daniels against Aries Priest and Darius Walker.
Introduced to the crowd as a newly signed RVRL wrestler; did not wrestle on this card.
Confronted the new RVRL Heavyweight Champion after the tournament final and set his client on him.
Attacked the new RVRL Heavyweight Champion immediately after the tournament final.

matches.note: First round of the RVRL Heavyweight title tournament. Aries Priest defeated "Reverend" Al Horton by pinfall.
First round of the RVRL Heavyweight title tournament. Colt Daniels defeated "The Motor City's Own" Bryan McCormick by pinfall (Colt .45).
First round of the RVRL Heavyweight title tournament. Jay Himalay defeated The Masked Krishna by pinfall (The Liberty Press).
First round of the RVRL Heavyweight title tournament. "Rabid" Rob Cole defeated Jake Evans by pinfall after a tiger driver.
Second round of the RVRL Heavyweight title tournament. Colt Daniels defeated Aries Priest by pinfall, with run-in help from newly signed Rick Russell against Priest's manager Darius Walker.
Second round of the RVRL Heavyweight title tournament. "Rabid" Rob Cole defeated Jay Himalay by pinfall after a distraction spot with a hidden foreign object.

matches.title: rvrl-2006-missourivalley
matches.note: Final of the RVRL Missouri Valley Heavyweight Championship tournament. Jay Himalay defeated Aries Priest to become the inaugural (2006 revival) champion, using a handful of powder and a fistful of tights.

matches.title: rvrl-2006-heavyweight
matches.note: Final of the RVRL Heavyweight Championship tournament. "Rabid" Rob Cole defeated Colt Daniels to become the inaugural (2006 revival) champion with an illegal foreign-object shot to the head.

notes: A single full card script covering RVRL's 2006 revival opener, an eight-man tournament crowning both the Heavyweight and Missouri Valley Heavyweight Championships; no other RVRL card survives in the held record.
